solver.kind: blind AI solver (separate agent, answer-free packet, rubric v2)

E038-01.notes: Stem asks to introduce the story the essay questions (the accident story). Only C names the accident origin; A is a generic claim about cookies, B is about inns, D is about chocolate in baking.

E038-02.notes: 'which she cooked meals' and 'that she cooked meals' leave the clause incomplete because no relative pronoun can fill an object role there. 'when' is temporal and has no time antecedent. 'where' correctly refers to the place (the inn).

flags: minor: the link between writing a cookbook and being a 'careful cook' is a little indirect; the phrase supports her professional, methodical credentials. A is still clearly the only defensible choice.
E038-03.notes: The phrase adds to the profile (dietitian, careful cook, cookbook author) that undercuts the accident story. B, C and D misstate what it does. Fact check: Toll House Tried and True Recipes was published in 1930, before the cookie, so this is accurate.

E038-04.notes: The idiom is 'be supposed to'. 'suppose to' drops the -d, 'supposing to' is ungrammatical, and 'supposed for' is unidiomatic.

E038-05.notes: The two clauses contrast: the story is appealing, yet it doesn't fit. Only 'Although' gives that concession. Because, Since and So all signal cause.

flags: minor: the claim that the recipe was printed in newspapers 'across New England' is plausible (it ran in Boston-area papers) but simplified.
E038-06.notes: C is the only concrete, specific evidence. A, B and D are vague or redundant. 'Within a few years' fits 'immediate hit' loosely, but it is the only specific choice.

E038-07.notes: The subject is 'The number', which is singular, so the verb is 'was'. 'are' and 'have been' are plural and also shift the tense away from the past-tense narrative.

E038-08.notes: 'used to' marks a past habit. 'use to' is missing the -d. 'were used to chop' would need 'chopping' to mean 'accustomed to', or it reads as a passive. 'usually to' is ungrammatical.

flags: minor: 'reportedly' could also correctly take no commas at all, but no choice offers that, so A is the only acceptable choice.
E038-09.notes: A paired comma set off the parenthetical adverb. B leaves a single comma between subject and verb, C puts a comma between adverb and verb, and D's semicolon cuts off the subject from its verb.

E038-10.notes: Only B gives a reason the accident story has lasted. Fact check on C: the Toll House Inn burned on New Year's Eve 1984, which is accurate but off-goal.
